title: Israeli strike and fire at a displacement camp in Tel al-Sultan, Rafah
body:
On the night of Sunday 26 May 2024, an Israeli strike hit the Tel al-Sultan area of western Rafah, where displaced Palestinians were sheltering in a tent camp, and a large fire broke out. Palestinian health officials said at least 45 people were killed, about half of them women and children. An early figure from Palestinian health workers had been at least 35 dead. The World Health Organization said the casualties absolutely overwhelmed field hospitals in the area.

The Israeli military confirmed the strike and said it hit a Hamas installation and killed two senior Hamas militants. Rear Admiral Daniel Hagari said two munitions of 17 kilograms each were fired and were too small on their own to ignite a fire, and that the military was investigating whether weapons had been stored in the area. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called the incident a tragic mishap.

The strike drew outrage, including from some of Israel's closest allies. It came two days after the International Court of Justice ordered Israel to halt its Rafah offensive. Separate shelling in the same district on the following Tuesday killed at least 16 Palestinians, according to Palestinian Civil Defence and Red Crescent figures reported at the time.
